chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Recording 26 tunes with Miguelito Valdes during the 1942 strike
summary: Miguelito's first solo job was at La Conga with Machito; during the strike they recorded 26 sides in two days with little pressure.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I see. All right. Your band started at La Conga in 1942.
Now, was it after or before you start at La Conga that Miguelito Valdes left Xavier Cugat?
When we start at La Conga because the first work, the first job, the solo job that Miguelito had was at
With you. Okay. In May ah June of 1942 then, there was a musicians' strike and Miguelito told me in 1975 that you had two days to record twenty-four or twenty-six tunes. Do you recall that?
Okay, tell me about that, Macho.
Oh! that was a tremendous thing. A beautiful experience. Miguelito was a genius. He knows so much about that music that it was easy to work with him and the musicians worked with him.
But you did have - - How were you able to pull that off? Twenty-six recordings in two days; What did you do, work around the clock?

No, you would be surprised. The musicians had such a good analysis about what we want that it was like a, it was like a picnic. It was no pressure, with all the difficulties for recording in those particular times, because it was wax, it wasn't like now that you have fourteen, twenty channels and somebody better be taking and you over-dubbing, and those kind of things.
